recentItems.title: Russian spy satellites may be helping Iran hit US targets in the Gulf
recentItems.description: Fourteen Russian spy satellites moved over a US military base in Saudi Arabia two days before a devastating attack by Iran. The timing and sequencing of the spacecraft gave them access to a large spectrum of data which, US officials and international intelligence sources say, helped Tehran conduct some of its most precise attacks against American assets. CNN's Tamara Qiblawi reports.

recentItems.title: Skyrocketing fuel prices spark protests around the globe
recentItems.description: Protesters are taking to the streets around the world to voice anger about skyrocketing fuel prices and rolling blackouts, as the now monthslong US war with Iran drives up the cost of energy globally.

recentItems.title: Trump 'threw a tantrum' during Kennedy Center call, Joyce Beatty says
recentItems.description: Democratic Congresswoman Joyce Beatty told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins that Trump “threw a tantrum” on a call about the future of the Kennedy Center and made things “personal” with her because she won in court earlier Tuesday.

recentItems.title: Sanders and Bannon sound AI alarm at ‘pro-human’ gathering
recentItems.description: Fears about the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence have bent the American political spectrum to the point that Sen. Bernie Sanders, the democratic socialist from Vermont, appeared on the same stage as Steve Bannon, the former Trump adviser and MAGA fundamentalist, at an event in Washington, DC, on Tuesday. CNN's Donie O'Sullivan reports.

recentItems.title: GOP lawmakers on why Congress isn’t acting now
recentItems.description: CNN’s Manu Raju asks lawmakers if they feel a sense of responsibility to regulate AI.

recentItems.title: Ed Sheeran’s opening acts all quit in solidarity with Macklemore
recentItems.description: Ed Sheeran’s international tour has been thrown into crisis, with one opening act, the rapper Macklemore, dropped from the tour’s US dates for his onstage support of Palestine, and all of the British singer’s other openers quitting to protest the removal.

recentItems.title: Kerry Kennedy pleads with Trump: leave the Kennedy Center alone
recentItems.description: Kerry Kennedy issues a direct plea to President Trump after the Kennedy Center's board voted to shutter the historic building indefinitely. The shutdown came hours after a judge blocked Trump's name from being added to the facade — a move the board claimed was the only way to save it. Speaking to Erin Burnett, Kennedy blasted the president: "We have real pain in our country... focus on your job."
